title: Francis de Sales
hook: a gentle bishop: nothing is so strong as gentleness
tomorrow: Vincent de Paul and Louise de Marillac

segments.voice: Yesterday, Philip Neri, the laughing saint with half a beard. Your line was cheerfulness strengthens the heart.

"A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger." That's a proverb in the King James Bible, and it sounds easy until someone is shouting. Then the grievous words come quickly. Today's figure is a bishop who, tradition says, had a hot temper by nature, and spent his life learning the soft answer instead. People came to call him the gentleman saint. A saying linked to his name goes something like this: nothing is so strong as gentleness, and nothing so gentle as real strength.

Francis de Sales was a Catholic priest, then a bishop, when Catholics and Protestants in his corner of Europe were deeply divided. Tradition says that as a young priest he was sent into a region that had become Protestant, and when people wouldn't come to hear him, he wrote short pages explaining his faith and slipped them under doors. Whatever you make of his arguments, notice the method: patient, quiet, personal. He wrote a book called Introduction to the Devout Life, as letters of advice to a woman living an ordinary life in the world. Its big idea: a life of prayer isn't only for monks and nuns. A soldier, a shopkeeper, a parent, a servant can each be devout in the life they already have. And the way there, again and again in his writing, is gentleness, with others and with yourself. When you fall short, he advises, don't rage at yourself. Pick yourself up the way you'd lift a friend who tripped. Harshness, in his view, just adds a second problem to the first. Paul lists gentleness among the fruit of the Spirit: "love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith". And in Matthew's Gospel, Jesus describes himself this way: "for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls." Gentleness here isn't weakness. It's strength that has decided not to crush.
screen: `A DEVOUT LIFE, RIGHT WHERE YOU ARE.`

segments.voice: Think of a hard conversation coming up, or one that keeps replaying, and let the other person's sharpest line arrive; notice where it lands, in the jaw, the chest, the hands. Breathe out slowly, and silently try one soft answer: not a surrender, just a sentence with no edge on it. If you pray, hold the proverb as you breathe: a soft answer turneth away wrath. If not, stay with the slower breath and the unclenched jaw.
Gentleman saint. The nickname for Francis de Sales, the bishop who taught that gentleness, with others and with yourself, is a kind of strength.
Your line: nothing so strong as gentleness. That goes for how you treat yourself, too. Day eight hundred seventy-eight, done.
